related_gaps.rationale: Which tasks owe pages does not establish acceptance for an adopted product.

gap_review: Read the three open gaps; none changes. This task adds one, service-acceptance, for what the held-out build found.

discoveries.summary: The held-out service build could not be graded by the workflow and scenario runners as shipped; the adopting agent rewrote them.

As first written, the rule still charged every new product command a brief: the add-product-command skill has each command add a workflow case, and harness/workflows.json, readiness.json and docs/PRODUCT.md are protected paths. The product's acceptance files now keep their receipt without forcing a brief.
Moving the serde default alone fails 27 tests, because schema 6 records with no tier reach the eight pages through it; the declared tier became optional and is resolved by schema version.

discovery_review: Three discoveries: the service-acceptance gap from the held-out build, the acceptance-file exemption the brief showed was needed, and why the default could not simply be flipped.

documentation.rationale: docs/ARTIFACTS.md defines the tiers by risk and the one standard page; docs/EVALUATION.md records the paired run and the held-out build; docs/COMPLETION.md, AGENTS.md, README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md describe the new default.

prompt.task: make no pages the default for any task away from policy paths, cut the standard tier to a brief before code, and drop the report page
prompt.task_noun: pages by risk: no pages by default and a brief only for policy changes
prompt.area: xtask's tiers and page sets (xtask/src/task_record.rs, artifacts.rs, size.rs, router.rs, handover.rs) and docs/ARTIFACTS.md
prompt.problem: every task over 100 lines owes two reviewed pages that a paired run found add 30 to 50 minutes and no accepted change on product work
prompt.reference: The small tier's gate in xtask/src/size.rs and the page sets in xtask/src/artifacts.rs

summary: Default to no pages, keep one brief for changes to policy, dependency and ceremony paths, drop the report page, and record the paired run that says why.

review.acceptance: The four named tests exist and pass: a_task_with_no_tier_owes_no_pages_at_any_size and a_standard_task_owes_only_a_brief_before_code (xtask/tests/ceremony.rs), a_pageless_task_is_refused_on_policy_paths_only (xtask/tests/tiers.rs) and next_offers_review_of_a_brief_without_requiring_it (xtask/tests/brief.rs). One acceptance item changed after the brief, as the ticket now says: the product's acceptance files are not refused for a small task (protected_cargo_and_ceremony_paths_force_standard covers both sides).
review.verification: cargo xtask check ci passed 9 of 9 (target/verification/ci.json); cargo xtask gaps --base harness/ship-clean --report target/verification/ci.json is ok with harness/transitions/pages-by-risk.json. Page: brief.html pass in round 1 (0 findings; two non-blocking notes in reviews.json). This task was judged by its own branch's gate: a brief, no report. The paired run's twelfth cell, redo under the full tier, had not finished when docs/EVALUATION.md was written and is marked so. GitHub Actions has not run; nothing is pushed.
review.assumptions: That pages do not help product work rests on five features every no-pages run already passed, one run per cell, one model; docs/EVALUATION.md states this and what a set with headroom would need. That a brief earns its cost on gate changes rests on two of three harness briefs finding defects, which is anecdote, not a comparison. Exempting goldens from the brief assumes the edit guard's approval and the receipt are enough review for a baseline change.
review.coverage: No test runs a real product task end to end under the new default; the experiment's no-pages arm ran without task records, so a small task with its record and review answers has been exercised only in fixtures. Nothing measures whether an optional review is ever taken. The service-acceptance gap is open.
